_doc.purpose: Recognition rows that ARE in the DB (auto-accepted at match time) but are demonstrably WRONG. The exporter drops these from the published badges. This is separate from data/processed/recognition_review.json, which holds matches that were never accepted and still await a human ruling.
_doc.why_a_config: src/build_db.py destroys and recreates the DB on every refresh, so recognition.id values are NOT stable across runs. Suppression is therefore keyed on (slug, source, matched_name), which is stable.
_doc.review_status: PROPOSED by the dashboard build on 2026-08-01, pending the owner's ruling. Each entry states the mechanism, not just the conclusion. Setting `active: false` restores the badges without touching code.
_doc.root_cause: norm_name() in src/enrich_recognition.py strips a stopword list before comparing names. Where stripping collapses two different restaurants onto the same string, the match is spurious yet still scores 0.9 with notes ' [exact name]'. match_confidence 0.9 therefore does NOT imply the names resemble each other.

suppress.reason: norm_name() strips the stopwords 'osteria', 'brooklyn' AND 'brasserie', so both 'Osteria Brooklyn' and 'Brasserie' normalise to the EMPTY STRING. osteria-brooklyn is the only one of the 648 participants that normalises to '', so it absorbed all 8 James Beard awards belonging to the Seagram Building's Brasserie (winner, 2000). None of these awards belong to Osteria Brooklyn.

norm_name() strips both 'bar' and 'cafe', collapsing 'Bar Boulud' and 'Cafe Boulud' onto 'boulud'. These two nominations (2009, 2014) belong to Bar Boulud, a different Dinex room. Cafe Boulud's own six James Beard rows (matched_name 'Cafe Boulud') are genuine and are NOT suppressed, nor is its Michelin 1 star.
